newsitem.title: USA: High Plains Wheat - Dealers shocked by seedings.
newsitem.headline: High Plains Wheat - Dealers shocked by seedings.

text.p: Grain dealers in the U.S. High Plains said they were shocked by Friday's USDA winter wheat seedings estimate, which suggested that wheat seedings were at a 19-year low.

Winter wheat seedings for the 1997 crop were estimated at 48.22 million acres, well below the average projection in the Reuter analysts survey of 51.40 million. Hard red winter wheat seedings were estimated at 34.1 million acres, down five percent from last year.
"They must have missed some of their survey area or added wrong," one Oklahoma dealer said. "This is absurdly low."

The low estimate triggered sharply higher opening calls in wheat futures, but grain dealers said they had not yet seen much cash movement. Only a few grain dealers were pushing bids, with one south central merchandiser tacking on an additional two cents per bushel to his bid.

Meanwhile, much of the central Plains remained under a mass of bitter cold air. Dealers in Kansas said much of the snow that fell Thursday had blown away, which could leave the crop vulnerable to winterkill.
Basis values in cents/bu against KCBT wheat, cash=dollars/bu.
(Note: H=KCBT March wheat futures. unq- unquoted, na - not applicable)
